A SubagentsPanel should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A SubagentsPanel should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../../theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

false

fit

true

overflowing

## Panel

It has a header along its top, reading its title in small, semibold text, with a little padding around it. The header is on the theme's raised surface and the panel's body on its base surface, so the header stands slightly apart from the body, contrasting with it only a little, with no line between them, and along its bottom a 1 pixel border in the body's own colour, as the SidebarScope's headers say.
It shows no count of what it lists.
It is only as tall as its contents need, taking no more of its sidebar's height.

## Concept

### Pitch

The bottom panel of the [RightSidebarScope](../index.md#right-sidebar-scope), beneath the referenced files and the understanding: the subagents and background commands the harness started for the running task, each shown in the colour of the mode that started it, with how long it has been running, so one that seems stuck can be seen and stopped.

### Shape

#### Description

It lists the background tasks the harness started for the run, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../../../scope/harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) keeps them: its subagents, the agents it started, and its background commands, the shell commands it ran in the background, such as a long build. A background task of any other kind isn't shown.
It is shown only once the run has started one, and takes no room before. One row per background task, in the order they started, subagents and commands together, each 24 pixels tall, 8 pixels in from the panel's edges: a spinner while it is at work, then a tick, a cross, or a dash for how it ended, done, failed, or stopped, beside a small icon for its kind, a robot for a subagent and a terminal for a command, in the theme's muted grey, then what it was started to do, in small text, cut off with an ellipsis, muted once it has ended. For a subagent that is its description, and for a command the command itself, on one line, in monospace. Its tooltip gives what it was started to do, and beneath, muted, its kind, "Subagent" or "Command", and what it is doing or how it ended. The panel is only as tall as its rows need, up to 30% of the sidebar's height, scrolling beyond that.

#### Elapsed

At the right of each row, 8 pixels in from the panel's edge, is how long it has been running, from when the harness said it started, in extra small muted tabular figures, as a task's elapsed time is written beside its status: "0:42", "12:05", "1:02:33". While it is at work it counts up every second; once it has ended it stops at how long it ran. What it was started to do is cut off before the time rather than running beneath it.

#### Stopping

A row at work can be stopped, from a Stop button: a small ghost button with a stop icon, 18 pixels square, which takes the place of its running time while the row is hovered, whose tooltip reads "Stop this subagent" or "Stop this command". Clicking it stops only that background task, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../../../scope/harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says: the task the run is for and every other background task carry on, and nothing else in the panel or the task's output changes. Once clicked, the button is disabled and the row's spinner stays until the harness notifies its end, when it shows a dash for stopped, as any stopped one does. A row that has ended has no Stop button, and neither does one whose run can't stop it on its own, as one whose input is already closed, where the task's own Cancel button stops everything still going.

#### By Mode

Each background task is shown according to the mode of the task that started it, as the [PromptModesScope](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) colours modes: its row has a bar 2 pixels wide down its left edge in that mode's colour, and its spinner and tick are drawn in it too, while a cross or dash keeps its own colour. A background task's mode is the mode its task was sent in, and for a step of a chain, the step's own: the spec step and a spec follow-up are Spec's, and the code step is Code's, never Chain's purple. Its tooltip names the mode, "Started by the Code task", "Started by the Spec step", and so on. A task whose mode isn't known, as one from the history saved before modes were, has no bar and keeps its spinner and tick in their own colours, its tooltip reading "Started by the task". A Chain task on its own, before its code step has been sent, is the chain's spec step, so its background tasks are Spec's and labelled "Spec".
While a chain runs, the panel keeps the background tasks of each of its steps, not only the step running: they are grouped by step, in the order the steps ran, each group headed by a small label in its mode's colour, "Spec", "Code", or "Spec follow-up", with the step running last. A task that isn't part of a chain has one group, and no label. Once the run is over, the sidebar slides back with them all, as it says.

34:Where the harness takes rules for what its tools may do, as Claude Code does with `--disallowedTools`, a run on the host is told what its mode keeps it off. A Code task is told it may not edit the spec location, and a Spec task the code location; the application puts back whatever changes there all the same, and says so in the task's output as a passive notice, never an error, as the [TaskTableScope](../../ui/components/task-table/index.md#task-table-scope) says. A Code task is also told it may not read the spec location, alongside that, so it reads the compiled reference instead, as the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) says. A question from the Ask tab always runs in a container, so it is never given this rule, nor any other telling it to keep off the spec location. This rule is only a nudge, and doesn't enforce anything, since a shell command can still read the files, and nothing puts anything back or stops the run when one does. A harness that takes no such rules is told nothing of either.
40:A run can also start work in the background that goes on after its turn ends: Claude Code's subagents, shell commands run in the background, such as a long build, and any other kind of background task it adds later. Every such task holds the run open, whatever its kind. The run keeps each background task that has started and not yet ended, by its id: one starts when the harness says a task has started, and ends when the harness notifies that task's end, whatever it ended as. A notification doesn't say what kind of task it is, so it is matched by id against those seen starting. The harness wakes the run when a background task ends, so it can act on what came of it.
41:Each background task is known by its kind, from what started it: a subagent, started by an Agent or Task tool call, or a command, a shell command run in the background. Its start is when the harness said it had started, so how long it has been running can be told. A single background task can be stopped while the run goes on, without ending the run or any other task: the harness is asked, on the run's input, to stop that task by its id, Claude Code with its stream-json control request for stopping a task. The task then ends when the harness notifies its end, as ever, as stopped, and the harness carries on with what came of it. Stopping one is never done by stopping the harness's process, and a run whose input is already closed, or whose harness can't be fed, can't stop one on its own.
42:A result no longer ends the task on its own. The run's last result is the first to come once every message sent has been taken in and no background task is still going. A result that comes before then, while a message sent hasn't been taken in or a background task is still going, is only an answer: the task keeps running, its input stays open, and more can still be sent to it. At the last result the run's input is closed, but the task is only shown as finished once the harness's process has exited as well, and it then finishes in the state of that last result; until the process exits, the task keeps running. A process that exits without a last result finishes the task as a run with no result does, failed. A run that is stopped closes its input and ends straight away, whatever is still going in the background, since its whole process group is ended with it.
54:Questions from the Ask tab share a separate conversation of their own, and when the project is opened they carry on the latest conversation among the questions saved with it. A question asked while another is running carries on a copy of that conversation, so questions running at the same time never write over each other. A conversation is only carried on in the project it began in, each open project keeping its own tasks' and questions' conversations while it is in the background. A spec lane or questions conversation from before its sessions were kept in the project, whose session the project's sessions folder doesn't hold, is still tried, and when the harness has no such session, the request is sent again at once as a new conversation, as below.

34:Where the harness takes rules for what its tools may do, as Claude Code does with `--disallowedTools`, a run on the host is told what its mode keeps it off. A Code task is told it may not edit the spec location, and a Spec task the code location; the application puts back whatever changes there all the same, and says so in the task's output as a passive notice, never an error, as the [TaskTableScope](../../ui/components/task-table/index.md#task-table-scope) says. A Code task is also told it may not read the spec location, alongside that, so it reads the compiled reference instead, as the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) says. A question from the Ask tab always runs in a container, so it is never given this rule, nor any other telling it to keep off the spec location. This rule is only a nudge, and doesn't enforce anything, since a shell command can still read the files, and nothing puts anything back or stops the run when one does. A harness that takes no such rules is told nothing of either.
40:A run can also start work in the background that goes on after its turn ends: Claude Code's subagents, shell commands run in the background, such as a long build, and any other kind of background task it adds later. Every such task holds the run open, whatever its kind. The run keeps each background task that has started and not yet ended, by its id: one starts when the harness says a task has started, and ends when the harness notifies that task's end, whatever it ended as. A notification doesn't say what kind of task it is, so it is matched by id against those seen starting. The harness wakes the run when a background task ends, so it can act on what came of it.
41:Each background task is known by its kind, from what started it: a subagent, started by an Agent or Task tool call, or a command, a shell command run in the background. Its start is when the harness said it had started, so how long it has been running can be told. A single background task can be stopped while the run goes on, without ending the run or any other task: the harness is asked, on the run's input, to stop that task by its id, Claude Code with its stream-json control request for stopping a task. The task then ends when the harness notifies its end, as ever, as stopped, and the harness carries on with what came of it. Stopping one is never done by stopping the harness's process, and a run whose input is already closed, or whose harness can't be fed, can't stop one on its own.
42:A result no longer ends the task on its own. The run's last result is the first to come once every message sent has been taken in and no background task is still going. A result that comes before then, while a message sent hasn't been taken in or a background task is still going, is only an answer: the task keeps running, its input stays open, and more can still be sent to it. At the last result the run's input is closed, but the task is only shown as finished once the harness's process has exited as well, and it then finishes in the state of that last result; until the process exits, the task keeps running. A process that exits without a last result finishes the task as a run with no result does, failed. A run that is stopped closes its input and ends straight away, whatever is still going in the background, since its whole process group is ended with it.
54:Questions from the Ask tab share a separate conversation of their own, and when the project is opened they carry on the latest conversation among the questions saved with it. A question asked while another is running carries on a copy of that conversation, so questions running at the same time never write over each other. A conversation is only carried on in the project it began in, each open project keeping its own tasks' and questions' conversations while it is in the background. A spec lane or questions conversation from before its sessions were kept in the project, whose session the project's sessions folder doesn't hold, is still tried, and when the harness has no such session, the request is sent again at once as a new conversation, as below.

The Subagents panel now lists background shell commands alongside subagents. Each row shows how long it has been running and has a Stop button. Every task also shows how long it has been under way next to its status label. `cargo check` is clean and the full test suite passes (504 passed, 1 ignored). I didn't run the app, and I haven't tried stopping a task against a real Claude Code run.

**One thing to check:** the stop message I send to Claude Code is `{"type":"control_request","request_id":"stop-N","request":{"subtype":"stop_task","task_id":"<id>"}}`. That format is from my memory of Claude Code's control protocol, not checked against its docs or a live run. If the field names are wrong, Stop won't do anything, and the row will stay greyed out until the task ends by itself.

**Panel** (`src/referenced_spec.rs`, `src/subagents.rs`)
- The header now reads "Subagents and commands".
- Subagents and commands share one list in the order they started. After the status icon there is a muted robot or terminal icon. A command shows the command it ran, in monospace on one line; I take that from its Bash tool call and fall back to the harness's description if I can't find it.
- The tooltip now starts with "Subagent" or "Command".
- At the right of each row is its running time ("0:42", "12:05", "1:02:33"), counting up every second and stopping once it ends. Hovering a running row replaces the time with an 18px ghost Stop button ("Stop this subagent" / "Stop this command").
- Clicking Stop sends the stop request on the run's input and nothing else. The button turns disabled and the spinner keeps going until the harness reports the end, then the row shows the stopped dash.
- There's no Stop button on rows that have ended, or when the run's input is closed or it can't take more input (Codex, OpenCode). That last case falls out of how those runs are set up.

**Harness** (`src/harness.rs`)
- A background task is a subagent when Claude Code reports it as `local_agent` and a command when it reports `local_bash`. Other kinds aren't shown.
- Stopping one never ends the harness's process.

**Task time** (`src/prompt_mode.rs`, `src/prompt_history.rs`)
- A task's start is recorded when it is sent, so building and compiling count. Its time stops when it's done, failed or cancelled.
- The time shows in the latest task's header and in each previous task's heading, including one running in the other lane.
- Start and end are now saved in each task's record (`startedAt` / `endedAt`). Older records don't have them, so those tasks show no time.

**Where I made a choice:**
- A subagent's or command's start time is when the app receives the harness's "started" message.
- The combined chain row (the one that groups a chain's steps) gets no time. Each step's own heading has one.

**Two things that happened during testing:**
- One test, `raw_prompt_opens_once_the_task_has_compiled`, failed once on a clipboard check. It passes on its own and passed on the full rerun, so it looks flaky rather than caused by this change.
- While checking that test, I briefly stashed the uncommitted changes. During that time something, probably the running app's mode guard, put back the stashed edits to the four spec files. They matched the stash exactly, so I reset those files and restored the stash; nothing was lost.

The spec and the prompt didn't disagree anywhere. The constraints are in `.suspense/history/1791107515-MonitorAndStopStuckAgents2.understanding.md`.

The Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need authorizing in your claude.ai connector settings, and the `backlog` MCP server didn't start (its program isn't on your PATH). None of them were needed here.
